submission.justification:
Algorithm-L3 with a 32 GeV threshold achieves the highest signal efficiency (87.648%) among all algorithms that meet the hard latency constraint. 

Algorithm-L1, while offering higher efficiency (91.861% at 32 GeV), has a latency of 5.8 us which exceeds the hard 4.0 us limit imposed by front-end buffer depth and therefore cannot be used. 

Algorithm-L2 meets the latency requirement (1.9 us) but achieves significantly lower efficiency (~73%) compared to Algorithm-L3.

Algorithm-L3 meets all requirements: latency of 3.1 us (well below 4.0 us limit), threshold within the 20-60 GeV range, operates at the allocated 8 kHz rate, and maximizes signal efficiency among viable options. The threshold of 32 GeV was determined through systematic simulation scanning, showing peak efficiency at this value.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L3 (sliding-window clustering with learned calibration) is one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency must not exceed 4.0 us
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L3 has a measured latency of 3.1 us per firmware_testbench_results.md, which is below the 4.0 us limit. Algorithm-L1 was excluded as it has 5.8 us latency.
Selected threshold of 32 GeV is within the specified range

requirements.requirement: Achieve highest possible signal efficiency at allocated rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L3 at 32 GeV achieves 87.648% efficiency, which is the highest among algorithms meeting the latency constraint. Systematic threshold scanning confirmed 32 GeV as optimal. The allocated rate of 8 kHz is maintained.
